To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a significant difference in perceptions of IS success between IS users and the IS staff.
IS staff and IS users have different perceptions of system success.
IS users and IS developers have different perspectives of IS success and that there is a need to improve existing measures to better represent the needs and perceptions of all stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the IS success measures of the provider and user differ and what can be done to improve these measures.
the measurement of software success and the differences in perception over the stakeholder groups of users and staff.
the development of an instrument to measure software development success.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IS success is a function of the perceptions of the IS users and IS providers.
IS staff and IS users have different perceptions of the same system and the success of the system is dependent upon the perspective of the individual.
IS success measures are not the same for all stakeholders and should not be measured by one instrument.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the success of ISs is a function of the perception of the stakeholders.
the IS staff and the IS user are two separate entities with different perceptions on what constitutes success.
the IS staff should be more concerned with the quality of the system, whereas the IS users are more interested in the functionality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IS users and IS developers have different perceptions of the success of an IS.
there is a need for a common set of measures to evaluate IS success.
the success of IS is not just a single measure.
